base_instruction: You are a helpful event planning assistant. Help the user plan a youth sports team end-of-season banquet by tracking attendees, their dietary needs, and logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates to restrictions throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm organizing the end-of-season banquet for my kid's soccer team. Can you help me plan the food?

Coach Rivera grew up in a Jain family in Gujarat
We're thinking of using the community center banquet hall, seats about 30
Emma from the team is coming too — her dad just confirmed. She's been on a strict keto diet for her epilepsy, doctor prescribed it

hidden_state.value: You are a parent organizing an end-of-season banquet for your kid's soccer team. You will introduce attendees and their backgrounds across several turns. Some constraints will be removed (misdiagnosis), some people will join late, and one person will leave but want a plate saved. At the end, you will share a caterer's buffet menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, friendly parent volunteer. You relay information about other families in third person (e.g., 'Marcus's mom just called me...', 'Aiden's mom told me...'). You never express frustration or impatience. You treat schedule changes and updates as normal coordination for a kids' event.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

ground_truth.answer: Chicken satay with peanut sauce: problematic for Aiden's saved plate (severe peanut allergy) and for Coach Rivera (Jain — no meat). Sushi platter with raw salmon and tuna: problematic for Coach Rivera (Jain — no fish) and Coach's wife (pregnant — no raw fish). Caesar salad with croutons: fine for everyone at the table — Marcus's celiac was a misdiagnosis, he can eat gluten now. Veggie spring rolls with sweet chili sauce: need to check ingredients for Coach Rivera (Jain — no root vegetables like onion/garlic), but otherwise fine. Pasta carbonara: problematic for Emma (keto — pasta is high carb) and for Coach Rivera (Jain — contains egg, and often contains garlic). The peanut sauce on the chicken satay must be excluded from Aiden's saved plate.

ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint removal. Key tracking challenges: (1) Coach Rivera is from a Jain family → Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (inferential chain). (2) Marcus's celiac disease is REMOVED mid-conversation (misdiagnosis confirmed). (3) Aiden EXITS the banquet but wants a saved plate (peanut allergy scope changes from table to saved plate only). (4) Coach's wife JOINS late with an inferential constraint (pregnant → no raw fish). (5) Emma JOINS late with keto constraint. At probe time, the agent must apply CURRENT state: Coach Rivera = Jain (no meat/fish/eggs/root veg), Coach's wife = pregnant (no raw fish), Emma = keto (no high carb), Aiden = peanut allergy (saved plate only). Marcus has NO restrictions. The Caesar salad is a trap — it looks problematic for celiac but that constraint was removed. The chicken satay tests both the Jain constraint (meat) and the scope-limited peanut allergy (saved plate).

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
